description:
File: crate-jmap-chat-client/src/methods/mod.rs:178-187 (custom Deserialize impl).

The custom `Deserialize` impl for `Patch<T>` maps:
- JSON `null` → `Patch::Clear`
- JSON value → `Patch::Set(v)`
- (Note: there is no "absent" arm in `deserialize`; that only happens with `#[serde(default)]` on the field, in which case the `Default` impl returns `Patch::Keep`.)

The struct-level rustdoc (mod.rs:103-128) tells callers to write:
```rust
#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Patch::is_keep")]
pub my_field: Patch<String>,
```

The two attributes are documented as "must" carry both. BUT:

If a downstream caller wraps `Patch<T>` in their own type and forgets `#[serde(default)]`, the absent-key case **does not produce `Patch::Keep`**. Instead it fails the deserialize entirely (no default). If they remember `#[serde(default)]` but forget `skip_serializing_if`, serialization fails at runtime with the custom-Serialize Error path (mod.rs:168-171).

This is exactly the "API shape that forces every caller to write the same boilerplate" pattern. Three failure modes:
- Forget `default`: every absent field rejects on parse, even though `Patch::Keep` is the intended absent value.
- Forget `skip_serializing_if`: every `Patch::Keep` panics at runtime with a `serde::ser::Error::custom("Patch::Keep cannot be serialized…")`.
- Forget BOTH: never even reaches the second failure because parse fails first.

The contract is correct as designed, but the boilerplate has no compile-time enforcement. A derive helper macro (`#[derive(JmapPatch)]`) is the canonical fix but a larger change. Smaller fixes:

1. Add a doctest that demonstrates the failure modes — at least callers reading rustdoc will see them.
2. Add a clippy-lint or rustc check note: not really feasible without a proc-macro.
3. Provide a `pub trait PatchField` with a blanket impl that requires the attributes to work, so the compiler errors guide the caller. (Tricky to implement.)
4. Wrap the `Patch<T>` in a `pub struct PatchField<T>(Patch<T>);` with `#[serde(transparent)]`-equivalent behavior and a `Serialize`/`Deserialize` pair that handles the absent case via `Option<T>` — but this defeats the point of `Patch<T>` existing.

Recommendation: doctest in mod.rs:113 showing both the right and wrong way, especially the "forget `default` → parse fails" case. The current doc says "must" but doesn't show the failure.

Caller impact: real. Anyone building a downstream extension to JMAP Chat that wants its own `*Patch` struct hits this. The fail-fast direction is correct (errors are loud), but the failure happens far from where the attribute was forgotten.
title: Patch<T> attribute boilerplate (\#[serde(default)] + skip_serializing_if) has no compile-time enforcement
